Remove the glottal-flow-derivative construct and the closure instant detection mechanism ceases to exist: there is no derivative to analyze for zero-crossings. This passes the removal test: the GCI construct cannot operate without the derivative.

The asymmetry-coefficient is defined as the ratio of rising-phase duration to falling-phase duration, where the rising and falling phases are identified by the sign of the first derivative of the glottal flow: rising phase is where g'(n) > 0, falling phase is where g'(n) < 0. The definition explicitly requires the first derivative of g(n) to locate phase boundaries. Remove the glottal-flow-derivative construct and the phase boundaries cannot be identified, making the asymmetry ratio impossible to compute. This passes the removal test.

Pitch-tracking is the process of linking pitch estimates across consecutive frames to produce a continuous pitch trajectory. Pitch-detection is the per-frame algorithm that identifies the fundamental period or frequency within a single frame. Remove pitch-detection and each frame loses its fundamental period estimate, making cross-frame linking impossible — pitch-tracking cannot operate without the per-frame detections it chains. The direction runs the higher-level process (pitch-tracking) to the lower-level component it depends on (pitch-detection).

payload.name: pressed-voice
payload.scope: People made pressed voice as a classification category to name the phonation mode of excessive glottal contact - hyperfunctional phonation - so that laryngology can tell it apart from modal and breathy phonation in voice-disorder assessment and voice therapy.

definition.body: Pressed voice (pressed phonation, hyperfunctional phonation) is a classification category for a mode of voiced phonation defined by a specific glottal configuration: the vocal folds are pressed together with excessive medial compression, so that each cycle carries a prolonged closed phase and an abrupt, steep opening. Its parameters are: (1) the glottal configuration - excessive medial compression of the folds with prolonged complete closure during each vibration cycle, (2) the cycle signature - a shortened open phase and a lengthened closed phase relative to the fundamental period (a high contact quotient, a low open quotient), a short rise time, and a steep flow declination, (3) the acoustic signature - a harsh, strained, or pressed timbre with reduced harmonic-to-noise contrast and reduced glottal airflow. It persists as a named mode of the phonation-mode taxonomy: documented in laryngology (spastic and hyperfunctional dysphonia, muscle-tension dysphonia), used in voice-disorder assessment and voice therapy, and maintained alongside modal, breathy, falsetto, creaky, and whisper phonation. e.g.: the pressed (hyperfunctional) category in a voice-disorder assessment of muscle-tension dysphonia; the pressed-voice label in a laryngoscopy report of spastic dysphonia; the pressed category in Sundberg's five-mode phonation inventory | not: creaky voice (low-frequency implosive vibration, a different mode); breathy voice (incomplete closure with noise leak, a different mode); modal phonation (complete closure at modal timing, a different mode) [formal: vox compressa | substrate: mind | horizon: generations | explicit: yes]

payload.name: phase-quotient
payload.scope: A voice-quality parameter expressing the proportion of any single phase duration (open, closed, contact) relative to the total glottal-cycle period, enabling standardized comparison of phase timing across speakers and conditions.

definition.body: Phase-quotient is a normalized voice-quality parameter that expresses the duration of a specific phase within the glottal cycle as a fraction of the total cycle period (T0). Given the phase duration D measured in milliseconds and the fundamental period T0, the phase quotient is D/T0, yielding a dimensionless value between 0 and 1. Its parameters are: (1) the phase duration D of the specific phase under consideration (e.g., open phase, closed phase, contact phase), (2) the glottal-cycle period T0 from pitch tracking, (3) the phase identification method (flow-based, EGG-based, or combined). A phase quotient near 0 indicates minimal time in that phase; near 1 indicates near-total occupancy. It persists as a standardized clinical parameter computed by voice-analysis software, documented in the Dewaele and Liljens-Forsberg parameter sets, and maintained in laryngology reference ranges. e.g.: open-quotient as reported in the Dewaele parameter set; closed-quotient values from the Liljens-Forsberg glottal source model; contact-quotient measured from an electroglottogram in a Praat analysis | not: glottal-cycle period T0 (the denominator, not the quotient itself); open-phase-duration (the raw duration in milliseconds, not the normalized ratio) [formal: quota phasei | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes]

payload.note: SERVES: contact-area is a clinical parameter measured by EGG transducers in laryngology practice. It quantifies the area of vocal-fold contact per cycle, reported as a diagnostic metric for glottal insufficiency, nodules, and other pathologies. The laryngology discipline maintains its standardized measurement protocol, reference ranges, and clinical interpretation for diagnosis and surgical planning.

The laryngology discipline maintains its standardized measurement protocol, reference ranges, and clinical interpretation for diagnosis and surgical planning.

SERVES: glottal-area-function is the time-varying waveform of vocal-fold contact area, estimated from EGG or glottal flow, used clinically in laryngology to assess vocal fold pathology including nodules, polyps, and paralysis. It persists as a diagnostic parameter in laryngology toolkits and clinical protocols.

SERVES: glottal-area-function is the time-varying waveform of vocal-fold contact area, estimated from EGG or glottal flow, used clinically in laryngology to assess vocal fold pathology including nodules, polyps, and paralysis. It persists as a diagnostic parameter in laryngology toolkits and clinical protocols.

SERVES: maximum-flow-derivative (MFD) is the peak rate of change of glottal airflow during the open phase, a clinical parameter used in laryngology to assess vocal fold stiffness and tissue health. It is measured in voice-analysis toolkits used in laryngology practice for diagnosing voice disorders and monitoring treatment outcomes.

SERVES: maximum-flow-derivative (MFD) is the peak rate of change of glottal airflow during the open phase, a clinical parameter used in laryngology to assess vocal fold stiffness and tissue health. It is measured in voice-analysis toolkits used in laryngology practice for diagnosing voice disorders and monitoring treatment outcomes.

SERVES: glottal-source-spectrum is the per-frame power spectrum of the glottal flow waveform, used in laryngology to characterize the glottal source's spectral shape — a steeply falling spectrum marks breathy phonation, a flatter spectrum indicates pressed phonation. It persists as a maintained diagnostic representation in laryngology voice-analysis toolkits.

SERVES: glottal-source-spectrum is the per-frame power spectrum of the glottal flow waveform, used in laryngology to characterize the glottal source's spectral shape — a steeply falling spectrum marks breathy phonation, a flatter spectrum indicates pressed phonation. It persists as a maintained diagnostic representation in laryngology voice-analysis toolkits.

SERVES: glottal-flow-declination-rate measures the average rate of decrease in glottal flow during the open phase, a clinical parameter used in laryngology to assess vocal fold mass and tissue stiffness. It is computed by voice-analysis toolkits used in laryngology practice for diagnosing voice disorders and monitoring treatment outcomes.

SERVES: glottal-flow-declination-rate measures the average rate of decrease in glottal flow during the open phase, a clinical parameter used in laryngology to assess vocal fold mass and tissue stiffness. It is computed by voice-analysis toolkits used in laryngology practice for diagnosing voice disorders and monitoring treatment outcomes.
